fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter." (Numbers 27:8). The sisters had asked for property among their father's brothers, and here the LORD tells Moses to say this to the Israelites. It becomes a rule for everyone, not just one family. I think five sisters walked out of that tent with a whole lot more than they asked for.

Careful, friend, this one flips the verse. The LORD tells Moses, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly." (Numbers 27:7). They had come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and asked for property among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:2-4). Moses brought their case to the LORD, and that's the answer that came back. I'd say the sisters got a stamp of approval, and I know a little something about waiting for one of those.

Duties sounds official, but that's not what the verse says. The LORD tells Moses, "You certainly must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers and transfer their father’s inheritance to them." (Numbers 27:7). The property is their inheritance, and it's given to them. Nobody handed these five a to-do list.

Right on, baker. "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers." (Numbers 27:9). The LORD's rule goes in order: son first, then daughter, then brothers. And the order keeps going, because the next verse covers what happens if there are no brothers (Numbers 27:10).
